| [THEORY-121](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-121.md) | Moral responsibility requires guidance control, moderate reasons-responsiveness of the agent's own actual-sequence mechanism, and not regulative control over alternative possibilities, so responsibility is compatible with causal determinism | Fischer and Ravizza (1998), reported second-hand: the book is unread. Fischer's own lawful summary ("Stories and the Meaning of Life", [LIT-689](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-689.md), read) states the core first-hand: guidance control, not regulative control, is the freedom-relevant condition; it is acting from one's own, moderately reasons-responsive mechanism; and it is compatible with causal determinism. McKenna and Coates ([LIT-291](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-291.md), §4.4 and supplement §B) and Talbert ([LIT-691](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-691.md), §2.3) report the analysis: Frankfurt-type cases move responsiveness from the agent to the mechanism actually at work; the mechanism must show regular, understandable receptivity to reasons, including moral ones, and some reactivity; and it is the agent's own when she has taken responsibility for it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-122](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-122.md) | Moral responsibility requires the normative competence to recognise and act on the True and the Good, which identification with one's own motives does not supply | Susan Wolf's Reason View, reported second-hand: the primary texts are unread. McKenna and Coates ([LIT-291](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-291.md), §4.3) report that for Wolf free will is the ability to act in accord with the True and the Good, an anchor outside the agent's psychology. Talbert ([LIT-691](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-691.md), §§3.1.1, 3.2) reports her case against deep-self or Real Self views and the JoJo case: JoJo identifies wholly with the cruel values his father raised him in, yet is not responsible, because he cannot appreciate that they are wrong. The claim is a necessary condition. It does not by itself say whether the ability must include being able to do otherwise; that is [THEORY-118](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-118.md). | Proposed |
